To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adversarially trained networks are not only sensitive to the input distribution, but also sensitive to the input perturbations, and this phenomenon is more pronounced for the robust accuracy than the clean accuracy, and this is a counter-intuitive phenomenon because it contradicts with the intuition that the robustness is a property of the model and should not change when we change the input data distribution
(1) Adversarial robust accuracy is sensitive to the distribution of the input data, and (2) The sensitivity of robust accuracy is different from the sensitivity of the clean accuracy.
Adversarial Robstness is sensitive to the distribution of input data, and the Bayes classifier is not robust to small perturbations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) How does input data distribution affect the adversarial training and robustness? (2) Can we make the robustness of neural networks less sensitive to the input distribution? (3) How to evaluate adversarial robustness on unseen input distribution? (4) Can we make adversarial training less sensitive to the data distribution?
a fundamental question: How does the input data distribution affect the robustness of neural networks?
a new aspect of adversarial robustness and provides a new perspective on the evaluation of adversarial robust models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adversarial robustness is not invariant to input data distributions.
, in general, adversarially trained neural networks are sensitive to input data distribution.
adversarial training is a data-dependent algorithm, in a sense that the adversarial robust accuracy of the trained model is sensitive to the data distribution on which the training is performed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adversarial robust accuracies of neural networks trained on a distribution can vary greatly when evaluated on a different but semantically-identifiable distribution, and the sensitivity to input data distributions should be taken into consideration when evaluating the robustness of adversarially trained neural networks.
adversarial training is not a panacea for the vulnerability of neural networks.
adversarial training can lead to a robust model, but the robustness can vary drastically across input distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the input distribution matters in adversarial robustness.
adversarial training is sensitive to the data distribution.
the robustness of adversarial trained models is not as stable as the clean accuracy, and thus we should be cautious in interpreting the robustness of neural networks.
